Once again, Proposition 8.3 can be proved in a more elementary way using equivariant cohomology, see [Z4, Proposition 5.3.14] (but this proof is specific to the characteristic- $0$ setting).

9 Identification of the dual group

At this point, we have constructed the convolution product $\star$ on
$\mathrm{P}_{{G_{\mathcal{O}}}}(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G},\mathbf{k})$ , a $\mathbf{k}$ -linear faithful exact functor $\mathsf{F}:\mathrm{P}_{{G_{\mathcal{O}}}}(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G},\mathbf{k})\to{\mathord{\mathrm{Vect}}}_{\mathbf{k}}$ ,
an associativity constraint, a commutativity constraint, and a unit
object $U={\mathbf{IC}}_{0}$ such that:

1.

$\mathsf{F}\circ\star=\otimes\circ(\mathsf{F}\otimes\mathsf{F})$ and $\mathsf{F}(U)=\mathbf{k}$ ;

2.

$\mathsf{F}$ maps the associativity constraint, the commutativity constraint and
the unit constraints of $\mathrm{P}_{{G_{\mathcal{O}}}}(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G},\mathbf{k})$ to the corresponding constraints of
${\mathord{\mathrm{Vect}}}_{\mathbf{k}}$ ;

3.

If $\mathsf{F}(L)$ has dimension 1, then there exists $L^{-1}$ such that
$L\star L^{-1}\cong U$ .

(For (3), one observes that for $L={\mathbf{IC}}_{\lambda}$ to
satisfy $\dim\mathsf{F}(L)=1$ , by Proposition 5.13 $\lambda$ must be orthogonal to each root $\alpha\in\Delta(G,T)$ ,
so $\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G}^{\lambda}=\{L_{\lambda}\}$ , and we can take $L^{-1}={\mathbf{IC}}_{-\lambda}$
since $-\lambda$ is dominant.)

Tannakian reconstruction (see Theorem 2.7) then gives us an affine group scheme $\widetilde{G}_{\mathbf{k}}$ over $\mathbf{k}$
and an equivalence $\mathsf{S}$ which fits in the following
commutative diagram:

$\textstyle{\mathrm{P}_{{G_{\mathcal{O}}}}(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G},\mathbf{k})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$ $\scriptstyle{\sim}$ $\scriptstyle{\mathsf{S}}$ $\scriptstyle{\mathsf{F}}$ $\textstyle{{\mathord{\mathrm{Rep}}}_{\mathbf{k}}(\widetilde{G}_{\mathbf{k}})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$ $\scriptstyle{\omega}$ $\textstyle{{\mathord{\mathrm{Vect}}}_{\mathbf{k}},}$

where $\omega$ is the forgetful functor. We now need to identify
$\widetilde{G}_{\mathbf{k}}$ .

paper.title: Notes on the geometric Satake equivalence
paper.abstract: These notes are devoted to a detailed exposition of the proof of the Geometric Satake Equivalence for general coefficients, following Mirkovic-Vilonen.
